items.X_name: Cadence: scans cleanly when read aloud
items.X_desc: Read the line aloud once and score its prosody. 10 = tight rhythm, balanced stresses, alliteration or repetition that makes the line feel finished and quotable. 5 = serviceable but unremarkable. 0 = syllable-padded, lopsided, or typographically clumsy so it stumbles in the mouth (awkward spaced colons, filler conjunctions, one element far longer than the others).
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when rhythm, repetition, or sound makes the line especially punchy when read aloud; score 0 when its cadence is inert, clumsy, or forgettable.

items.X_name: List whose final item subverts the preceding ones
items.X_desc: Applies to enumerations. Score the shape of the list. 10 = the first items establish an expected register and the last item breaks it, so the turn arrives exactly at the end. 5 = a coherent list with a mild escalation. 0 = a flat list of equally weighted items with no turn, or a turn placed in the middle where it deflates. Non-list items score 5.
items.Y_name: List/enumeration structure with a pattern-breaking final item
items.Y_desc: Score the presence and effectiveness of a short list (2+ items) where the final item breaks the pattern set by the earlier items, producing a twist. A 10: a clean list whose last item clearly subverts or undercuts the expectation set by the prior items. A 0: no list structure, or a list whose items are flat, interchangeable restatements with no capstone twist.

items.X_name: Ironic reversal
items.X_desc: Give 10 when the surface statement sets up an expectation that a second reading sharply undercuts; give 0 when the wording has only one straightforward meaning.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the literal wording turns back on itself to expose a clear comic contradiction; score 0 when the statement is entirely literal and unreversed.

items.X_name: Playful exploitation of the stated word-count constraint
items.X_desc: For hashtags that stipulate a word count, score how the line treats that budget. 10 = the constraint is made part of the joke, for example hyphen-stacking to smuggle extra concepts into the legal count, or spending the exact budget so every word is load-bearing. 5 = the count is met unremarkably. 0 = the count is overrun or badly undershot with nothing gained, so the line reads as if it ignored the game.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the requested word-count format feels deliberately exploited as part of a natural, complete phrase; score 0 when the wording feels truncated, padded, or accidentally shaped by the constraint.

items.X_name: Title transformation
items.X_desc: Give 10 when a recognizable title is altered into a fresh, coherent comic premise; give 0 when the title is merely copied or the reference is unintelligible.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when a recognizable title is transformed into a new phrase with a coherent, specific comic meaning; score 0 when only a superficial word substitution or title echo is present.

items.X_name: Concrete visuality
items.X_desc: Give 10 when the wording evokes a specific, vivid scene or object that can be pictured immediately; give 0 when it remains abstract or visually indeterminate.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the tweet evokes a vivid, specific scene that can be pictured instantly; score 0 when it remains vague, abstract, or generic.

items.X_name: Full comic payoff realized in text alone, not offloaded to a link

A 10: the text alone delivers the complete joke with nothing missing. A 0: the tweet includes a link or references unseen media and the text alone is flat or incomplete without it.

Score how much work the import does beyond recognition. 10 = the borrowed phrase is bent, recontextualized, or turned so the old frame says something new in this contest's world. 5 = lightly repurposed but the meaning is unchanged. 0 = reproduced verbatim as a quotation with no alteration and no new angle, or no borrowed phrase is present and none is needed (score 5 in that case and note it).
items.Y_name: Original construction vs. single-word-swap into a famous title
items.Y_desc: Score how much original content the line adds beyond a single mechanical word-swap into an already-famous title's exact structure. A 10: built largely from scratch, or the source phrase is altered substantially so most of the comic content is original. A 0: the line just swaps one or two words into an unmistakable famous title while keeping its exact remaining structure, and the swap itself is the entire joke.

items.X_name: Transformation depth beyond a one-token swap
items.X_desc: For title/name mashups and puns, score how much idea the substitution adds beyond naming its source. 10 = the swapped element carries a genuine second thought, so the line would still be funny to someone who half-recognizes the source. 5 = a clean substitution that produces one modest joke. 0 = a single letter or word is changed and the entire payload is source recognition, with no observation attached.
items.Y_name: Familiar-phrase skeleton with one incongruous-register substitution
items.Y_desc: Score whether the tweet takes a familiar fixed phrase/structure from one domain (religious, patriotic, sentimental, wartime) and substitutes one element from a jarringly different-register domain, using the swap to reveal something about a persona. A 10: a clear familiar-phrase skeleton with one element swapped for a jarringly incongruous substitute that recontextualizes the whole phrase. A 0: no recognizable borrowed phrase/structure is being subverted at all.

items.X_name: Single clean payload: no links, spare hashtags, or meta
items.X_desc: Score the item as a delivery vehicle after ignoring the contest hashtag and the single required @midnight mention. 10 = nothing but the joke; the eye goes straight to the payload. 5 = one minor distraction (stray punctuation, doubled spacing). 0 = the line carries a URL, additional unrelated hashtags, self-promotion, or flattery of the show itself, so attention is split away from the joke.
items.Y_name: Engagement with the specific prompt vs. format-generic meta-joke
items.Y_desc: Score how tightly the joke's content is bound to THIS specific hashtag prompt, versus being a generic joke about the contest format/act of tweeting itself that could be copy-pasted under almost any other hashtag with no loss of meaning. A 10: the joke could only make sense for this exact prompt/category. A 0: the joke is about tweeting/the account/the show itself and barely engages the prompt's actual topic.
